concepts.title: Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle
concepts.definition: The sector of a circle is the region enclosed by two radii and their arc, and the segment is the region between a chord and its arc; their areas are fractions of the circle's area, decided by the central angle - sector area equals angle over 360 times pi r squared.
concepts.key_idea: Angle decides the share: 90 degrees earns a quarter of pi r squared.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh111.txt section 12.1 (areas of sector and segment of a circle)

solution_steps.explain: Multiply by pi r squared for the sector area.

concepts.title: Length of an Arc of a Circle
concepts.definition: The length of an arc subtending angle theta at the centre is the same fraction of the circumference: arc equals angle over 360 times 2 pi r.
concepts.key_idea: The arc's share of the boundary equals the angle's share of the full turn.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh111.txt section on length of an arc

concepts.title: Areas of Combinations of Plane Figures
concepts.definition: Real designs - flower beds on square corners, circular tablecloths on tables, sectors in designs - are combinations of plane figures; their areas are found by adding or subtracting the basic circle, square and triangle areas as the design dictates.
concepts.key_idea: Add the wanted parts, subtract the unwanted: composition solves composite areas.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh111.txt section 12.2 (areas of combinations of plane figures)

Use pi r squared, side squared or half base times height as needed.
